eventMetadata.context_description: California Gov. Gavin Newsom leads trader consensus at 27.4% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, reflecting his national profile from post-2024 clashes with the Trump administration, term-limited status freeing him after 2026 midterms, and early book tour stops in New Hampshire and South Carolina signaling presidential ambitions. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez trails at 8.3% on strong progressive appeal and youth polling edges, while former VP Kamala Harris sits at 6.8% despite some surveys showing her ahead amid lingering 2024 name recognition. Sen. Jon Ossoff recently surged to 6.5% following a viral April 18 video criticizing Trump foreign policy, overtaking Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro (3.9%). With a fragmented field ahead of 2026 midterms, consolidation could hinge on fundraising dominance, key endorsements, swing-state primary polling, and midterm results reshaping party dynamics.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by end of April?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and April 30, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for April 30, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects a 77.5% market-implied probability that Strait of Hormuz traffic will not return to normal by April 30, driven by persistent US naval blockade of Iranian ports—implemented April 13 amid the ongoing Iran conflict—and Iran's reciprocal threats to reimpose restrictions. Ship-tracking data from MarineTraffic and SynMax indicates daily transits remain at under 10% of pre-war norms (roughly 135 vessels), with single-digit volumes even after Iran's April 17 "complete reopening" announcement during a fragile 10-day ceasefire. Heightened insurance premiums, crew safety concerns, and recent vessel U-turns underscore risk aversion, sustaining oil supply disruptions despite brief price plunges below $91 per barrel. Key catalysts include potential ceasefire extension talks and US enforcement actions before month-end.

title: Peru Presidential Election Winner
description:
General elections are scheduled to be held in Peru on April 12, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who wins the next Peruvian Presidential election. 

This market includes any potential second round. 

If the results are not known definitively by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of this election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely on the official results as reported by the Peruvian government, specifically the National Office of Electoral Processes (Oficina Nacional de Procesos Electorales, ONPE) (https://www.onpe.gob.pe/elecciones/) and the National Jury of Elections (Jurado Nacional de Elecciones, JNE) (https://portal.jne.gob.pe/portal/)

eventMetadata.context_description: Keiko Fujimori leads trader consensus at 65.5% implied probability to win Peru's presidency following the April 12-13 first-round vote, where she secured 17.06% with 93.5% of ballots tallied, advancing to the June 7 runoff. Roberto Sánchez Palomino holds 22.6% odds amid his narrow 12.01% edge over Rafael López Aliaga's 11.92% for second place, as the National Office of Electoral Processes (ONPE) resolves remaining challenged records amid delays from ballot delivery failures and fraud allegations by right-wing protesters. Pre-election polls showed Fujimori consistently ahead in a fragmented field of 35 candidates, with no outright majority possible; her Popular Force party's congressional strength and past runoff experience position her favorably against a leftist challenger like Sánchez from Together for Peru.
